blogs.title: Teaching Old Dogs New Tricks: How Orthogonal Finetuning Keeps AI Models from Forgetting
blogs.description: This post introduces the core concept of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) in an accessible way. It explains the fundamental problem of finetuning large AI models—they tend to 'forget' what they learned during pretraining—and how OFT solves this by using mathematical rotations that preserve the relationships between neurons. The post uses everyday analogies (like adjusting the angle of a camera without changing the scene's fundamental structure) to explain how OFT maintains a model's core knowledge while adapting it to new tasks.

blogs.title: Your Dog in Paris: How AI Learns to Generate Custom Subjects in New Contexts
blogs.description: This post focuses on the subject-driven generation application of OFT. It explains how, given just a few photos of your dog, the model can generate images of your dog in entirely new contexts—wearing a yellow shirt on the streets of Paris, for example. The post highlights how OFT outperforms existing methods like DreamBooth and LoRA in preserving the subject's identity while following text prompts more accurately. It includes visual examples showing how OFT maintains stable performance across many training iterations, unlike methods that collapse or lose subject identity over time.

blogs.title: Beyond Text Prompts: Giving AI Precise Visual Control with OFT
blogs.description: This post explores the controllable generation capabilities enabled by OFT. It explains how the method allows users to guide image generation using additional signals like edge maps, segmentation maps, or facial landmarks, alongside text prompts. The post describes how OFT achieves more accurate control than ControlNet and T2I-Adapter while using fewer parameters and requiring less training data. It also introduces the novel control consistency metric proposed in the paper, which measures how well generated images match the input control signals.

blogs.title: Why Angles Matter More Than Magnitude: The Surprising Math Behind AI's Semantic Understanding
blogs.description: This post dives into the intuitive insight that powers OFT: the directions (angles) of neurons in a neural network carry most of the semantic meaning, while magnitudes are largely irrelevant. It explains the paper's toy experiment showing that angular information alone can reconstruct images almost perfectly. The post also draws parallels to 2D Fourier transforms, where phase information (angular) preserves the semantics of an image far better than magnitude. This fundamental observation motivates why finetuning neuron directions through orthogonal transformations is both effective and safe for preserving pretrained knowledge.

blogs.title: LoRA vs. OFT: Two Paths to Efficient AI Model Finetuning
blogs.description: This post compares OFT with the popular LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) method, highlighting their fundamentally different approaches to parameter-efficient finetuning. While LoRA adds low-rank weight updates to preserve pretrained knowledge, OFT applies orthogonal transformations that provably maintain the angular structure between neurons. The post explains the trade-offs in parameter efficiency, convergence speed, and finetuning stability, and discusses when each method might be preferred. It also covers the COFT (Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning) variant, which adds an explicit constraint on how far the model can deviate from pretrained weights.
